pretreatments.description: Thermal pretreatment was carried out by heating sludge samples (50 ml) at temperatures ranging from 110 °C to 150 °C for 20 min in an oil bath (Daihan Science, Korea) to enhance sludge disintegration without improving methane yield significantly.

Alkaline pretreatment was conducted by adding 5 N solutions of Ca(OH)_2, KOH, and NaOH to 50 ml of WAS, with pH adjusted to values ranging from 8 to 13. This method was evaluated for COD solubilization and sludge disintegration, showing the highest DD at pH 13 with NaOH (40.10%).

Ultrasonication was performed on 50 ml of WAS using a VCX-750 sonicator at 20 kHz frequency and 20% amplitude, resulting in microbubbles formation and cavitation effects similar to HC but requiring specific equipment and energy analysis.

Hydrodynamic cavitation (HC) was applied using a stainless steel hydrocavitator with an orifice plate having 27 holes of 1 mm diameter, operating with upstream and downstream pressures of 0.7 and 0.07 MPa to generate microbubbles and disintegrate sludge efficiently.

Combined pretreatment (HC + alkaline) was examined as a synergistic approach to sludge disintegration, showing higher DD (53.47%) than individual methods, with a specific energy consumption of 1200 kJ/kg TS compared to 3600 kJ/kg TS for ultrasonication.
